newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National dips on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National dips on profit-taking.

text.p: Abbey National Plc was among the biggest decliners in the UK's FTSE 100 index on Tuesday, though dealers said the drop reflected no more than limited profit-taking and noted that trade in the stock was thin.
The stock, which hit a peak of 866p on May 1, was down 5-1/2p or 0.7 percent at 832-1/2 by 0812 GMT, standing out as the FTSE touched record highs. Volume was just 183,849 shares.

Dealers were sceptical about one notion that the decline could reflect a knee-jerk reaction to expectations of a UK interest rate rise later today, which could dampen the housing market where Abbey National is heavily involved.
The UK Treasury said it brought forward its monetary policy meeting due on Wednesday, sparking talk that a rate rise could be imposed later today.

Dealers pointed out that Abbey shares had been squeezed higher as investors sought the stock as a substitute for recently-floated Alliance & Leicester Plc, most of whose shares remain in the hands of private investors.
"It has had a tremendous run, there has been a massive bear squeeze in the stock," said one senior sales trader. "There is just a slight bit of profit-taking."
He added that a UK interest rate rise should already have been discounted.
Lloyds TSB Plc, also heavily exposed to the domestic housing market and which was also squeezed sharply higher when A&L made its debut, was down 5p at 551 in volume of 886,431 shares.
